{"at":"2026-09-25T22:38:45Z","note":"**Decision: every file the ticket loop writes is bookkeeping, named file by file** — per ticket <tickets>/<t-id>/{manifest.toml, journal.jsonl, atoms/10-intent.md, atoms/<profile checklist file>}, and lock files directly inside the claims dir. Not the whole ticket directory: anything else a person keeps there (an attachment, an extra atom) stays bound; nothing under the Warrants root is ever a ticket record. Why the checklist and intent too: they are a person's durable document, but a document ABOUT the work — a tick is work state written down, a note is context — never the source a gate runs over; a ticket is never compiled/authorized/verified/resolved and no Warrant, deliverable or Gate Definition reads one (promote copies text into a Warrant, whose atoms stay bound). Excluding only journal+claims fixes nothing: done and note write checklist and intent every time. A content-aware rule (tick vs reword) was rejected: hand edits are honoured as written and one edit can carry both. What a verdict could depend on, said: war check validates ticket structure (ticket.checklist-malformed / item-duplicate / blocker-unknown / blocker-cycle), so a war-check or battery receipt says nothing about ticket files written after it — the same stated limit t-22fd gave authority records; war check run now still reads them. Declared inputs are not narrowed. Found on the way: the claims dir writes its own .gitignore on every claim, so locks never reached git; the claims exclusion is for a claims dir whose ignore file is gone. Written in docs/RESOLVING.md 'Working a ticket does not move the tree (t-5d82)' after t-22fd's subsection, and one paragraph in docs/TICKETS.md.","item":"i-5278"}
